subproblem.title: Integrating the truncated superlevel estimates over levels (moment factor, Tonelli, layer cake)
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 2 and ℓ ∈ ℕ, and let μ be a measure on E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Borel σ-algebra) that is finite on compact sets. Let h: E → ℝ be continuous, nonnegative and compactly supported. Let D, K: E → ℝ be nonnegative, with D μ-integrable and K μ-integrable on tsupport h. Let γ: ℝ → ℝ be C¹ and nondecreasing with 0 ≤ γ ≤ 1 and γ = 0 on (−∞, 0], and let C ≥ 0 and ε > 0. Put p := n/(n − 1), M_s := {x : h(x) > s}, γ' := deriv γ, and write μ(M_s) for the real measure. Suppose that for every t ≥ 0, μ(M_{t+ε}) ≤ C·μ(M_t)^{1/n}·(∫γ'(h − t)D dμ + ∫_{M_t}K dμ). Then ((n − 1)/n)·∫_{M_ε}(h^p − ε^p) dμ ≤ C·(∫_{M_0}(h + ε)^p dμ)^{1/n}·∫(D + hK) dμ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (h D K : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (γ : ℝ → ℝ) (C ε : ℝ), 2 ≤ n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → Continuous h → HasCompactSupport h → (∀ x, 0 ≤ h x) → (∀ x, 0 ≤ D x) → Integrable D μ → (∀ x, 0 ≤ K x) → IntegrableOn K (tsupport h) μ → ContDiff ℝ 1 γ → Monotone γ → (∀ s, 0 ≤ γ s ∧ γ s ≤ 1) → (∀ s, s ≤ 0 → γ s = 0) → 0 ≤ C → 0 < ε → (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → μ.real {x | t + ε < h x} ≤ C * (μ.real {x | t < h x}) ^ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((∫ x, deriv γ (h x - t) * D x ∂μ) + ∫ x in {x | t < h x}, K x ∂μ)) → ((n : ℝ) - 1) / n * ∫ x in {x | ε < h x}, (h x ^ ((n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - 1)) - ε ^ ((n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - 1))) ∂μ ≤ C * (∫ x in {x | 0 < h x}, (h x + ε) ^ ((n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - 1)) ∂μ) ^ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∫ x, (D x + h x * K x) ∂μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra. For a set A of finite μ-measure, μ(A) is the real number μ.real A, and μ[A] ∈ [0, ∞] is the extended value. ∫ denotes Bochner integrals (0 for non-integrable integrands), ∫⁻ lower Lebesgue integrals of [0, ∞]-valued functions, ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] the map y ↦ max(y, 0), dt Lebesgue measure on ℝ, and γ' = deriv γ. Source: steps 5–6 of the parent proof (the last page of the proof of Simon 5.7, with Simon 4.11), for an arbitrary measure and abstract nonnegative data D, K. Notation: p := n/(n − 1), b := 1/(n − 1). Since n ≥ 2: p > 1, b > 0, p − 1 = b, p/n = b and 1/p = (n − 1)/n. K₀ := tsupport h; M_s := {x : h(x) > s}; P(t) := ∫ γ'(h − t)D dμ; R(t) := ∫_{M_t} K dμ; Q_ε := ∫_{M_0} (h + ε)^p dμ; J := ∫ (D + hK) dμ.

1. (h and μ.) K₀ is compact, so μ[K₀] < ∞. h is continuous, so every M_s is open (Borel), and {(x, u) ∈ E × ℝ : u < h(x)} is open in E × ℝ. For s ≥ 0, x ∈ M_s gives h(x) > s ≥ 0, so x ∈ support h ⊆ K₀; thus M_s ⊆ K₀ and μ[M_s] < ∞. h is bounded: 0 ≤ h ≤ m for some m. μ is σ-finite (finite on compacts in the σ-compact space E). So Tonelli's theorem applies to μ ⊗ dt and to ν ⊗ dt, where ν := μ restricted to K₀ (a finite measure).
2. (γ.) γ' is continuous (γ ∈ C¹) and γ' ≥ 0 (γ nondecreasing). For s < 0, γ ≡ 0 on the open neighbourhood (−∞, 0) of s, so γ'(s) = 0. For a ≥ 0:
 (B1) ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal(γ'(a − t)) dt = ofReal(γ(a)) ≤ 1.
 Indeed, for t > a the integrand is ofReal(γ'(a − t)) = 0. On (0, a] the integrand is continuous and nonnegative, so its lower integral is ofReal(∫_0^a γ'(a − t) dt). Substituting s = a − t and using the fundamental theorem of calculus for the C¹ function γ, ∫_0^a γ'(a − t) dt = ∫_0^a γ'(s) ds = γ(a) − γ(0) = γ(a), since γ(0) = 0. Finally γ(a) ≤ 1. (SimonGMT Chapter04.lintegral_deriv_shifted_cutoff.) Also, for a ≥ 0:
 (B2) ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} 1_{t < a} dt = (Lebesgue measure of (0, a)) = ofReal(a).
3. (Integrability.) Fix t ≥ 0. Since h(x) − t ∈ [−t, m − t] for all x and γ' is continuous, x ↦ γ'(h(x) − t) is continuous and bounded. As D is integrable, γ'(h − t)D is integrable and P(t) ≥ 0. K is integrable on K₀ ⊇ M_t, so R(t) is the integral of an integrable nonnegative function and R(t) ≥ 0. The function hK vanishes off K₀ (h = 0 there). On K₀ it is the bounded continuous h times the integrable K, so it is integrable on K₀, hence on E. So D + hK is integrable, J = ∫ D dμ + ∫ hK dμ, and J ≥ 0. (h + ε)^p is continuous, hence bounded on the compact K₀ ⊇ M_0, and μ[M_0] < ∞; so it is integrable on M_0 and Q_ε ≥ 0. Likewise h^p − ε^p is bounded on M_ε ⊆ K₀, hence integrable on M_ε. It is ≥ 0 there because h > ε > 0 and y ↦ y^p is increasing on [0, ∞).
4. (Moment factor; parent step 5.) Fix t ≥ 0. On M_t, h + ε > t + ε ≥ 0, so (t + ε)^p ≤ (h + ε)^p. Hence
 (t + ε)^p μ(M_t) = ∫_{M_t} (t + ε)^p dμ ≤ ∫_{M_t} (h + ε)^p dμ ≤ ∫_{M_0} (h + ε)^p dμ = Q_ε.
 The last step holds because M_t ⊆ M_0 and the integrand is nonnegative and integrable on M_0. Raise both nonnegative sides to the power 1/n. Use (xy)^{1/n} = x^{1/n} y^{1/n} for x, y ≥ 0, and ((t + ε)^p)^{1/n} = (t + ε)^{p/n} = (t + ε)^b since t + ε ≥ 0. This gives
 (t + ε)^b μ(M_t)^{1/n} ≤ Q_ε^{1/n}.
5. (Weighted level estimate (5.a).) Multiply the hypothesis at t ≥ 0 by (t + ε)^b ≥ 0. Then use step 4 with C ≥ 0 and P(t) + R(t) ≥ 0:
 (t + ε)^b μ(M_{t+ε}) ≤ C·[(t + ε)^b μ(M_t)^{1/n}]·(P(t) + R(t)) ≤ C Q_ε^{1/n} (P(t) + R(t)).
6. (Integration over levels.) For each t > 0, apply the monotone map ofReal to (5.a) and integrate over t ∈ (0, ∞); monotonicity of ∫⁻ needs no measurability. Use ofReal(xy) = ofReal(x) ofReal(y) for x ≥ 0 and pull out the finite constant ofReal(C Q_ε^{1/n}):
 L := ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal((t + ε)^b μ(M_{t+ε})) dt ≤ ofReal(C Q_ε^{1/n}) · ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal(P(t) + R(t)) dt.
7. (Right side: Tonelli.) Let t > 0. Off K₀, h = 0, so γ'(h − t) = γ'(−t) = 0 and x ∉ M_t. Hence P(t) = ∫_{K₀} γ'(h − t)D dμ and R(t) = ∫_{K₀} 1_{M_t} K dμ. Both integrands are integrable and nonnegative, so ofReal of each integral is the lower integral of ofReal of the integrand:
 ofReal(P(t) + R(t)) = ofReal(P(t)) + ofReal(R(t)) = ∫⁻ [ofReal(γ'(h(x) − t)) ofReal(D(x)) + 1_{h(x) > t} ofReal(K(x))] dν(x).
 The integrand is a.e.-measurable for ν ⊗ dt on K₀ × (0, ∞): (x, t) ↦ γ'(h(x) − t) is continuous, {t < h(x)} is open, and D, K are a.e.-strongly measurable for ν. Apply Tonelli, then (B1) and (B2) with a = h(x) ≥ 0:
 ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal(P(t) + R(t)) dt = ∫⁻ [ofReal(D(x)) ofReal(γ(h(x))) + ofReal(K(x)) ofReal(h(x))] dν(x) ≤ ∫⁻ [ofReal(D(x)) + ofReal(h(x)K(x))] dν(x)
 ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(D) dμ + ∫⁻_{K₀} ofReal(hK) dμ = ofReal(∫ D dμ) + ofReal(∫_{K₀} hK dμ) = ofReal(∫ D dμ + ∫ hK dμ) = ofReal(J).
 This uses integrability and nonnegativity (step 3), ∫_{K₀} hK dμ = ∫ hK dμ (hK = 0 off K₀), and ofReal(x) + ofReal(y) = ofReal(x + y) for x, y ≥ 0.
8. (Left side: translation, Tonelli, layer cake = Simon 4.11.) For u > 0, μ[M_u] < ∞, so ofReal(u^b μ(M_u)) = ofReal(u^b)·μ[M_u]. Lebesgue measure is translation invariant and t ↦ t + ε maps (0, ∞) onto (ε, ∞), so L = ∫⁻_{(ε,∞)} ofReal(u^b) μ[M_u] du. Write μ[M_u] = ∫⁻ 1_{u < h(x)} dμ(x) and apply Tonelli (the integrand is measurable on E × ℝ):
 L = ∫⁻ (∫⁻_{(ε,∞)} ofReal(u^b) 1_{u < h(x)} du) dμ(x).
 If h(x) ≤ ε the inner integral is 0. If h(x) > ε it equals ofReal(∫_ε^{h(x)} u^b du) = ofReal((h(x)^{b+1} − ε^{b+1})/(b + 1)) = ofReal((h(x)^p − ε^p)/p). By step 3 (h^p − ε^p is integrable and nonnegative on M_ε) and 1/p = (n − 1)/n:
 L = ofReal(1/p) · ∫⁻_{M_ε} ofReal(h^p − ε^p) dμ = ofReal(((n − 1)/n) ∫_{M_ε} (h^p − ε^p) dμ).
 (SimonGMT Chapter04.layerCake_rpow with a = ε, α = p gives the same identity.)
9. (Conclusion.) By steps 6–8, ofReal(((n − 1)/n) ∫_{M_ε} (h^p − ε^p) dμ) ≤ ofReal(C Q_ε^{1/n}) · ofReal(J) = ofReal(C Q_ε^{1/n} J), because C Q_ε^{1/n} ≥ 0 and J ≥ 0. Since C Q_ε^{1/n} J ≥ 0 and ofReal y ≤ ofReal z with z ≥ 0 implies y ≤ z:
 ((n − 1)/n) ∫_{M_ε} (h^p − ε^p) dμ ≤ C (∫_{M_0} (h + ε)^p dμ)^{1/n} ∫ (D + hK) dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Moment factor: (t+ε)^p μ(M_t) ≤ ∫_{M_t}(h+ε)^p ≤ Q_ε, hence (t+ε)^{1/(n−1)} μ(M_t)^{1/n} ≤ Q_ε^{1/n}
Multiply the hypothesis by (t+ε)^{1/(n−1)}: (t+ε)^{1/(n−1)} μ(M_{t+ε}) ≤ C Q_ε^{1/n}(P(t) + R(t)) for all t ≥ 0
Integrate over t ∈ (0, ∞) as lower integrals; Tonelli on (μ⌞tsupport h) ⊗ dt with ∫_0^∞ γ'(a − t) dt = γ(a) ≤ 1 (FTC) and ∫_0^∞ 1_{t<a} dt = a gives ∫_0^∞(P + R) dt ≤ ∫(D + hK)
Translation u = t + ε, Tonelli and layer cake (Simon 4.11): ∫_0^∞ (t+ε)^{1/(n−1)} μ(M_{t+ε}) dt = ((n−1)/n)∫_{M_ε}(h^p − ε^p)
Return to real numbers through ofReal, using that the right side is nonnegative

subproblem.title: Letting the level shift ε ↓ 0 and absorbing the moment factor
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 2 and ℓ ∈ ℕ, and let μ be a measure on E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Borel σ-algebra) that is finite on compact sets. Let h: E → ℝ be continuous, nonnegative and compactly supported, and let C ≥ 0 and J ≥ 0. Put p := n/(n − 1) and M_s := {x : h(x) > s}. Suppose that for every ε ∈ (0, 1], ((n − 1)/n)·∫_{M_ε}(h^p − ε^p) dμ ≤ C·(∫_{M_0}(h + ε)^p dμ)^{1/n}·J. Then (∫h^p dμ)^{(n−1)/n} ≤ (n/(n − 1))·C·J.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (h : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (C J : ℝ), 2 ≤ n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → Continuous h → HasCompactSupport h → (∀ x, 0 ≤ h x) → 0 ≤ C → 0 ≤ J → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 → ((n : ℝ) - 1) / n * ∫ x in {x | ε < h x}, (h x ^ ((n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - 1)) - ε ^ ((n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - 1))) ∂μ ≤ C * (∫ x in {x | 0 < h x}, (h x + ε) ^ ((n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - 1)) ∂μ) ^ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * J) → (∫ x, h x ^ ((n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - 1)) ∂μ) ^ (((n : ℝ) - 1) / n) ≤ (n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - 1) * C * J
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra; ∫ denotes Bochner integrals; powers y^q of nonnegative reals are real powers (Real.rpow, so 0^q = 0 for q ≠ 0). Source: steps 7–8 of the parent proof ("letting ε ↓ 0" at the end of the proof of Simon 5.7). Notation: p := n/(n − 1), which is > 1 since n ≥ 2. K₀ := tsupport h is compact, so μ(K₀) < ∞. M_s := {x : h(x) > s} is open since h is continuous, and M_s ⊆ K₀ for s ≥ 0. Choose m ≥ 0 with 0 ≤ h ≤ m (h is continuous with compact support). Q := ∫ h^p dμ, a(ε) := ∫_{M_ε} (h^p − ε^p) dμ, Q_ε := ∫_{M_0} (h + ε)^p dμ, and ε_k := 1/(k + 1) ∈ (0, 1] for k ∈ ℕ, so ε_k → 0.

1. (Integrability.) h^p is continuous (p > 0) and vanishes wherever h = 0, in particular off K₀. So it is continuous with compact support, hence μ-integrable, and Q ≥ 0. Every function below is measurable (a continuous function times the indicator of an open set).
2. (First limit.) Put F_k := 1_{M_{ε_k}} (h^p − ε_k^p), so a(ε_k) = ∫ F_k dμ. If x ∈ M_{ε_k}, then h(x) > ε_k > 0, hence 0 ≤ h(x)^p − ε_k^p ≤ h(x)^p; otherwise F_k(x) = 0. So |F_k| ≤ h^p, which is integrable. Pointwise, F_k(x) → h(x)^p. If h(x) > 0, then ε_k < h(x) for all large k; for those k, F_k(x) = h(x)^p − ε_k^p → h(x)^p − 0 = h(x)^p, because y ↦ y^p is continuous at 0 with 0^p = 0. If h(x) = 0, then x ∉ M_{ε_k} for every k, so F_k(x) = 0 = 0^p = h(x)^p. By dominated convergence, a(ε_k) → ∫ h^p dμ = Q.
3. (Second limit.) Put G_k := 1_{M_0} (h + ε_k)^p, so Q_{ε_k} = ∫ G_k dμ. For x ∈ M_0, (h(x) + ε_k)^p → h(x)^p by continuity of y ↦ y^p on [0, ∞); for x ∉ M_0, G_k(x) = 0. Hence G_k → 1_{M_0} h^p pointwise. Since ε_k ≤ 1 and M_0 ⊆ K₀, 0 ≤ G_k ≤ (m + 1)^p · 1_{K₀}, which is integrable because μ(K₀) < ∞. By dominated convergence, Q_{ε_k} → ∫ 1_{M_0} h^p dμ = ∫ h^p dμ = Q, using h^p = 0 off M_0. The map y ↦ y^{1/n} is continuous on [0, ∞) (exponent 1/n > 0) and Q_{ε_k} ≥ 0, so Q_{ε_k}^{1/n} → Q^{1/n}.
4. (Passing to the limit.) The hypothesis with ε = ε_k ∈ (0, 1] gives ((n − 1)/n) a(ε_k) ≤ C Q_{ε_k}^{1/n} J for every k. By steps 2–3 the left side tends to ((n − 1)/n) Q and the right side to C Q^{1/n} J. Non-strict inequalities are preserved in the limit, so ((n − 1)/n) Q ≤ C Q^{1/n} J.
5. (Absorption.) Put A := (n/(n − 1))·C·J. Then A ≥ 0 because C ≥ 0, J ≥ 0 and n/(n − 1) > 0. If Q = 0, then Q^{(n−1)/n} = 0^{(n−1)/n} = 0 ≤ A, since (n − 1)/n ≠ 0. If Q > 0, multiply step 4 by n/(n − 1) > 0 to get Q ≤ A·Q^{1/n}. Divide by Q^{1/n} > 0 to get Q^{1 − 1/n} = Q/Q^{1/n} ≤ A, where 1 − 1/n = (n − 1)/n. In both cases (∫ h^{n/(n−1)} dμ)^{(n−1)/n} ≤ (n/(n − 1))·C·J. (SimonGMT Chapter04.rpow_one_sub_le_of_le_rpow_mul with M = Q and a = 1/n performs this step.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Dominated convergence along ε_k = 1/(k+1): ∫_{M_{ε_k}}(h^p − ε_k^p) → ∫h^p (dominated by h^p)
Dominated convergence: ∫_{M_0}(h + ε_k)^p → ∫h^p (dominated by (max h + 1)^p 1_{tsupport h}); continuity of y ↦ y^{1/n}
Pass to the limit in the hypothesis: ((n−1)/n)Q ≤ C Q^{1/n} J with Q = ∫h^p
Q = 0 is trivial; for Q > 0 divide by Q^{1/n}: Q^{(n−1)/n} = Q^{1−1/n} ≤ (n/(n−1)) C J

subproblem.title: Smooth level truncation turns the superlevel inequality into a distribution-function estimate
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ and let V be a rectifiable n-varifold in E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} whose weight μ = μ_V is finite on compact sets. Let U ⊆ E, let H: E → E be locally μ-integrable on U, and let C ≥ 0. Assume (S): every g: E → ℝ that is C¹ on U, nonnegative, and compactly supported with tsupport g ⊆ U satisfies ∫_{{g≥1}} g dμ ≤ C(∫g dμ)^{1/n}∫(|∇^M g| + g|H|) dμ. Let h: E → ℝ be C¹ on all of E and nonnegative, with compact support, tsupport h ⊆ U, and |∇^M h| μ-integrable. Let ε > 0 and t ≥ 0. Let γ: ℝ → ℝ be C¹ and nondecreasing with 0 ≤ γ ≤ 1, γ = 0 on (−∞, 0] and γ = 1 on [ε, ∞). Write M_s := {x : h(x) > s}, μ(M_s) for the real measure of these sets, and γ' := deriv γ. Then μ(M_{t+ε}) ≤ C·μ(M_t)^{1/n}·(∫γ'(h − t)|∇^M h| dμ + ∫_{M_t}|H| dμ). Here 1/n means the real exponent (n)⁻¹, which is 0 when n = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ) (U : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (H : Ambient n ℓ → Ambient n ℓ) (h : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (γ : ℝ → ℝ) (C ε t : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts V.weight → LocallyIntegrableOn H U V.weight → 0 ≤ C → (∀ g : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 g U → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ U → (∀ x, 0 ≤ g x) → ∫ x in {x | 1 ≤ g x}, g x ∂V.weight ≤ C * (∫ x, g x ∂V.weight) ^ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∫ x, (‖V.tangentialGradient g x‖ + g x * ‖H x‖) ∂V.weight) → ContDiff ℝ 1 h → HasCompactSupport h → tsupport h ⊆ U → (∀ x, 0 ≤ h x) → Integrable (fun x ↦ ‖V.tangentialGradient h x‖) V.weight → ContDiff ℝ 1 γ → Monotone γ → (∀ s, 0 ≤ γ s ∧ γ s ≤ 1) → (∀ s, s ≤ 0 → γ s = 0) → 0 < ε → (∀ s, ε ≤ s → γ s = 1) → 0 ≤ t → V.weight.real {x | t + ε < h x} ≤ C * (V.weight.real {x | t < h x}) ^ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((∫ x, deriv γ (h x - t) * ‖V.tangentialGradient h x‖ ∂V.weight) + ∫ x in {x | t < h x}, ‖H x‖ ∂V.weight)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra; μ = μ_V = V.weight; for a set A of finite measure, μ(A) is the real number μ.real A. All integrals ∫ are Bochner integrals (value 0 for non-integrable integrands), so integrability is checked wherever integrals are compared or split. p_x = (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection is the orthogonal projection onto T_xV, a continuous ℝ-linear map; ∇f(x) = gradient f x = (toDual ℝ E)⁻¹(Df(x)) is the Riesz representative of the Fréchet derivative; ∇^M f(x) = V.tangentialGradient f x = p_x(∇f(x)); γ' = deriv γ; e := (n : ℝ)⁻¹ ≥ 0 (e = 0 when n = 0, since 0⁻¹ = 0). Source: steps 1–4 of the parent proof (the truncation step at the end of the proof of Simon 5.7), with the particular cut-off ψ replaced by an arbitrary γ having the listed properties. Notation: K₀ := tsupport h, M_s := {x : h(x) > s} for s ∈ ℝ, g(x) := γ(h(x) − t), P := ∫ γ'(h − t)|∇^M h| dμ, R := ∫_{M_t} |H| dμ, I := ∫ (|∇^M g| + g|H|) dμ.

1. (γ.) γ is C¹, so γ' is continuous. γ is nondecreasing, so γ'(s) ≥ 0 for every s (Mathlib Monotone.deriv_nonneg).
2. (Sets of finite measure.) K₀ is compact because h has compact support, so μ(K₀) < ∞ (μ is finite on compacts). h is C¹, hence continuous, so every M_s is open, hence Borel. If s ≥ 0 and x ∈ M_s, then h(x) > s ≥ 0, so h(x) ≠ 0 and x ∈ support h ⊆ K₀. Thus M_s ⊆ K₀ and μ(M_s) ≤ μ(K₀) < ∞ for s ≥ 0; in particular M_t and M_{t+ε} have finite measure.
3. (Admissibility of g.) g = γ ∘ (h − t) is C¹ on E as a composition of C¹ maps, hence C¹ on U. g ≥ 0 because γ ≥ 0. If g(x) ≠ 0 then h(x) − t > 0 (otherwise h(x) − t ≤ 0 and γ(h(x) − t) = 0), so h(x) > t ≥ 0 and x ∈ support h. Hence support g ⊆ support h ⊆ K₀; as K₀ is closed, tsupport g ⊆ K₀. So g has compact support and tsupport g ⊆ K₀ ⊆ U, and the hypothesis applies to g:
 (A1) ∫_{{g ≥ 1}} g dμ ≤ C (∫ g dμ)^e · I.
 Moreover g is continuous with compact support, hence μ-integrable.
4. (Pointwise relations.) (i) 0 ≤ g ≤ 1_{M_t}: for x ∈ M_t, g(x) ≤ 1; for x ∉ M_t, h(x) − t ≤ 0, so g(x) = 0. (ii) g = 1 on M_{t+ε}: there h(x) − t > ε, so γ(h(x) − t) = 1; hence M_{t+ε} ⊆ {g ≥ 1}. (iii) Chain rule: h is differentiable at x and γ is differentiable at h(x) − t, so Dg(x) = γ'(h(x) − t)·Dh(x). The Riesz map (toDual ℝ E)⁻¹ is ℝ-linear, so ∇g(x) = γ'(h(x) − t)∇h(x). The projection p_x is linear, so ∇^M g(x) = γ'(h(x) − t)∇^M h(x). Taking norms and using γ' ≥ 0 gives |∇^M g(x)| = γ'(h(x) − t)|∇^M h(x)| for every x ∈ E.
5. (Integrable majorant.) h is continuous with compact support, so 0 ≤ h ≤ m for some m ≥ 0. For every x, h(x) − t lies in the compact interval [−t, m − t], where the continuous γ' is bounded by some L. So x ↦ γ'(h(x) − t) is continuous with 0 ≤ γ'(h(x) − t) ≤ L. Since |∇^M h| is μ-integrable, so is γ'(h − t)|∇^M h| (a bounded continuous factor times an integrable function), and P ≥ 0. H is locally μ-integrable on U and K₀ ⊆ U is compact, so H is μ-integrable on K₀ (Mathlib LocallyIntegrableOn.integrableOn_compact_subset). Hence |H| is μ-integrable on the measurable set M_t ⊆ K₀, so 1_{M_t}|H| is μ-integrable with ∫ 1_{M_t}|H| dμ = R ≥ 0. Therefore F := γ'(h − t)|∇^M h| + 1_{M_t}|H| is μ-integrable and ∫ F dμ = P + R.
6. (Left side.) g ≥ 0 is integrable on {g ≥ 1} and M_{t+ε} ⊆ {g ≥ 1}. The set integral of a nonnegative function is monotone in the set, so by 4(ii), and because M_{t+ε} is measurable with finite measure,
 ∫_{{g ≥ 1}} g dμ ≥ ∫_{M_{t+ε}} g dμ = ∫_{M_{t+ε}} 1 dμ = μ(M_{t+ε}).
7. (Mass factor.) By 4(i) and the integrability of g and of 1_{M_t}, 0 ≤ ∫ g dμ ≤ ∫ 1_{M_t} dμ = μ(M_t). Since e ≥ 0, y ↦ y^e is nondecreasing on [0, ∞), so 0 ≤ (∫ g dμ)^e ≤ μ(M_t)^e.
8. (Energy factor.) By 4(i) and 4(iii), 0 ≤ |∇^M g| + g|H| ≤ γ'(h − t)|∇^M h| + 1_{M_t}|H| = F pointwise. F is integrable (step 5), and the integral is monotone when the smaller function is nonnegative and the larger is integrable. This needs no separate proof that |∇^M g| + g|H| is integrable (Mathlib integral_mono_of_nonneg), and gives 0 ≤ I ≤ ∫ F dμ = P + R.
9. (Conclusion.) Combine step 6, (A1), steps 7–8, C ≥ 0, (∫ g dμ)^e ≥ 0, I ≥ 0 and μ(M_t)^e ≥ 0:
 μ(M_{t+ε}) ≤ ∫_{{g ≥ 1}} g dμ ≤ C (∫ g dμ)^e I ≤ C μ(M_t)^e I ≤ C μ(M_t)^e (P + R).
 This is μ(M_{t+ε}) ≤ C μ(M_t)^{1/n} (∫ γ'(h − t)|∇^M h| dμ + ∫_{M_t} |H| dμ). ∎
proof_key_steps: g := γ(h − t) is admissible for (S): C¹, nonnegative, support ⊆ {h > t} ⊆ tsupport h ⊆ U, compact support
Pointwise: 0 ≤ g ≤ 1_{M_t}, g = 1 on M_{t+ε}, and |∇^M g| = γ'(h − t)|∇^M h| (chain rule, linearity of the Riesz map and of p_x, γ' ≥ 0)
Left side of (S) for g is ≥ ∫_{M_{t+ε}} g = μ(M_{t+ε}); (∫g)^{1/n} ≤ μ(M_t)^{1/n} by g ≤ 1_{M_t}
Integrable majorant F = γ'(h − t)|∇^M h| + 1_{M_t}|H| (γ' bounded on the range of h − t; H integrable on compact tsupport h ⊆ U) gives ∫(|∇^M g| + g|H|) ≤ P + R
Combine the three bounds using C ≥ 0 and nonnegativity of all factors
